audit.name: Post Office Road
audit.source_family: 2026 RFL Championship official club walk (rugby-league.com competition page + Wikipedia 2026 RFL Championship) plus dedicated Featherstone Rovers / Post Office Road research
audit.current_tenant_status: Featherstone Rovers Rugby League Limited entered administration on 15 Dec 2025; the RFL confirmed on 9 Jan 2026 that the club would not be granted membership or entry to the merged 20-club 2026 Championship (confirmed directly against the RFL's own current Betfred Championship club list, which does not include Featherstone). The club is therefore NOT currently in any professional RFL division. The ground itself (current sponsor name 'The Millennium Stadium' since 2020) appears to remain in use: per a Yorkshire Post headline and an Insider Media headline (both title/snippet only -- full articles returned HTTP 403 on fetch, so treated as SEARCH_RESULT not FETCHED_URL) Featherstone Rovers Women continue playing there in 2026 and Wakefield Council granted the ground a new premises licence after a community campaign; the administrator is reported to be pursuing a return of the men's team for 2027. Ownership is unresolved between two retained Wikipedia pages: the 'Post Office Road' infobox states Owner/Operator = Featherstone Rovers, while the 'Featherstone Rovers' club page states the club sold the ground to the local council in February 1988 -- this contradiction was not resolved and is reported honestly rather than picked.

evidence.note: Administration timeline, 9 Jan 2026 RFL exclusion, 1959 record attendance 17,531, claim that ground was sold to the council in Feb 1988
Infobox capacity 6,954 (359 seated), Owner/Operator listed as Featherstone Rovers, current sponsor name 'The Millennium Stadium', Wakefield A.F.C. listed as a 2024-25 secondary tenant
Lists Post Office Road at 9,850 with no date/context attached -- this is the figure Package 06 already holds
Official RFL current Championship club list -- Featherstone Rovers absent, confirming non-membership
RFL's own statement on the exclusion decision, seen only as a search snippet, not fetched
Reports a new premises licence and continued use by Featherstone Rovers Women in 2026 -- page fetch returned HTTP 403, so only the search snippet was reviewed
Headline reports administrator working toward a 2027 return -- page fetch returned HTTP 403, so only the search snippet was reviewed
Lists capacity as 9,850, seen only via search summary

audit.notes: Both retained capacity figures (6,954 and 9,850) clear the 1,000-capacity threshold, so this does not change resolved_state, but the specific capacity_max value Package 06 holds (9,850) is not confirmed current -- genuinely conflicting, undated retained sources exist for both figures and I could not resolve which is correct. Recommend the builder treat this as an open capacity question rather than accept either figure as newly proven. Per SHARED-BRIEF rule 4, the two 403 fetch failures are recorded as blocked fetches, not converted into negative findings.

evidence.note: Package 06's STADIUM coverage statement records this row as accounted for by PREM Rugby (audited under RUGBY_UNION_GROUND).

audit.name: White Hart Lane Community Sports Centre
audit.source_family: London Skolars club-history research plus Wikipedia 'White Hart Lane Community Sports Centre' and Haringey Council's own New River leisure-centre page (operator) | Haringey Council operator page (New River Sport & Fitness) + official tenant-club (London Skolars) matchday page + Wikipedia infobox citation-provenance check + first-hand groundhopper account
audit.current_tenant_status: London Skolars remain the ground's rugby league tenant but withdrew from RFL-affiliated professional competition (League 1) at the end of the 2023 season; since 2024 they have played in the amateur/semi-pro Southern Conference League, not any RFL-recognised division. As of 2026 this venue therefore has no RFL Championship/League 1 tenant at all -- separately, RFL League 1 itself no longer exists as a distinct competition for 2026 (merged into the Championship, see source-families.jsonl), so there is no RFL League 1 for this venue to belong to either way. Confirmed via the club's own recent Southern Conference League coverage (TotalRL) that London Skolars still play out of this ground. Other tenants (Haringey Rhinos rugby union, Enfield and Haringey Athletic Club, Wood Green Weightlifting Club, Haringey Cycling Club) are outside rugby league scope. Operator confirmed as Haringey Council (New River Sport and Fitness / New River Leisure Centre) via the council's own website; that page describes the athletics track but does not itself state a spectator capacity figure for the stadium. | Council-operated community sports centre (Haringey Council, currently branded 'New River Sport & Fitness'), also known as White Hart Lane Community Sports Centre / New River Stadium, Wood Green. Tenants: London Skolars (rugby league, since 1995), Haringey Rhinos (rugby union), Enfield and Haringey Athletic Club (athletics — this club also uses Lee Valley Athletics Centre, already held at 6,750, and the QEII Stadium, Enfield), Wood Green Weightlifting Club and Park View F.C. The council's own current facility page presents the site as a gym/fitness/tennis/athletics-track/football community centre and does not describe it as a spectator stadium or give any capacity figure.

evidence.note: States grandstand holds approx. 1,000 of the 5,000 total capacity; lists London Skolars, Haringey Rhinos, Enfield and Haringey Athletic Club, Wood Green Weightlifting Club and Haringey Cycling Club as tenants
Confirms Haringey Council as operator of the New River site and describes the 8-lane floodlit athletics track; does not state a spectator capacity figure
Confirms London Skolars competing in the Southern Conference League (amateur tier), not an RFL-recognised division, seen via search summary
Confirms the club withdrew from professional/RFL leagues at the end of 2023 and joined the Southern Conference League for 2024, seen via search summary, not directly fetched
Raw wikitext: infobox capacity '5,000' and the body-text grandstand figure of '~1,000' both carry no citation; the References section is an empty {{Reflist}}.

Official tenant-club (London Skolars) matchday guide: 'The main stand seats 1,040 fans comfortably' with terrace standing 'only made available on special occasions when the main stand is full.' No total ground capacity of 5,000 appears anywhere on the club's own page.

First-hand groundhopper account: normal capacity is 1,000 ('only the big stand is open to spectators'); for one special event the terracing was safety-certified to raise capacity to 2,500 — not 5,000.

Current council operator page confirms the athletics track (8-lane floodlit, long/triple jump, high jump, pole vault) but gives no grandstand or spectator capacity figure and does not name an athletics club.

audit.notes: 5,000 capacity is corroborated, not newly proven -- it is only ever stated by Wikipedia and pages that appear to derive from it; no official club/council/governing-body page giving a numeric spectator capacity was found despite fetching the council's own operator page. Confidence should stay LOW/MEDIUM, not be upgraded to HIGH, per SHARED-BRIEF rule 5 (third-party corroboration is never 'official'). | As with Queensway, the held 5,000 figure traces to an uncited Wikipedia infobox. Every source that actually describes real current operation — the tenant club's own matchday guide (1,040 seats, terracing opened only rarely) and a first-hand account of a safety-certified special-event capacity of 2,500 — is well short of 5,000. On the athletics dimension specifically: Enfield and Haringey AC treats this as one of three venues it uses, and the current council operator page markets the site purely as a community leisure/athletics-track facility with no stated spectator capacity at all. No fetched page states a credible current total capacity, so no replacement number is invented, but 5,000 should not be treated as reliable. Full rugby-league attendance history is Researcher A's territory.

audit.name: Queensway Stadium
audit.source_family: Welsh Athletics facility directory (welshathletics.org) + current operator pages (Freedom Leisure / Wrexham County Borough Council) + Wikipedia/Wikidata infobox citation-provenance check + North Wales Crusaders club history
audit.current_tenant_status: Council-owned athletics stadium and leisure centre in Caia Park, Wrexham, operated by Freedom Leisure in partnership with Wrexham County Borough Council. Current primary tenant is Wrexham Athletics Club (8-lane 400m international-standard track); also home to FC Queens Park (football). Former rugby league tenant North Wales Crusaders played there 2017-2021 before relocating to Stadiwm Eirias, Colwyn Bay (already held separately in EXISTING-ESTATE.txt at 6,080). It is confirmed NOT Wrexham AFC's Racecourse Ground.

evidence.note: Raw wikitext: infobox capacity '8,256' carries no citation anywhere in the article; the References section is an empty {{reflist}} template.
Wikidata's capacity statement is sourced only as 'imported from English Wikipedia (oldid=803304099)' — circular, no independent primary source.

The tenant club's own article describes the Queensway ground physically as 'two small all-seater stands on one side overlooking a rugby pitch and a running track' and gives NO capacity figure for Queensway at all — unlike the 15,500 stated for the club's previous Racecourse Ground and 6,080 for its current Eirias Stadium ground, both of which the same article does quote a figure for.
First-hand groundhopper account of a North Wales Crusaders match at Queensway naming actual attendances at the venue as ranging from 'a few hundred to several hundred spectators'.
Current operator's own page describes the venue as a council leisure centre with an international athletics track; gives no spectator capacity figure.
Welsh Athletics facility page confirms Wrexham Athletic Club as home club and the 8-lane 400m track; gives no spectator capacity figure.

audit.notes: The held 8,256 LOW-confidence figure traces to a single, uncited Wikipedia infobox value with no independent corroboration found anywhere — not on the operator's own site, not on Welsh Athletics, not on Wrexham.com's own history page for the venue. Every source that actually describes the physical stand ('two small all-seater stands') or reports real attendances ('a few hundred to several hundred') is inconsistent with a capacity in the thousands, let alone 8,256. Per the ABSOLUTE RULES we are not inventing a replacement figure since no fetched page states one — but the held figure should be flagged/downgraded rather than relied on. web.archive.org fetch of an archived council page was blocked by tool restriction (RESEARCH_BLOCKED on that one lead, not a negative finding).
